We provide advanced inspection tools, metrology systems, process solutions, and computational analytics that make electronics possible, tackling complex challenges. From electron and photon optics to machine learning and data analytics, we seek perfection at the most fundamental level of matter in the universe. About Marvell
Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities.
At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead.
Your Team, Your Impact
Marvell's IT Project Management Office (PMO) is the backbone of how our global IT organization plans, governs, and delivers work from infrastructure modernization programs to digital workplace and enterprise application initiatives. Day to day, the team tracks project status against milestones, runs stage-gate governance reviews, coordinates vendor SOWs and budgets, and keeps cross-functional stakeholders aligned from kickoff through go-live. This governance discipline allows Marvell's IT function to execute large number of concurrent initiatives spanning all BUs and sites worldwide without losing visibility or accountability. As part of this team, you'll get a direct view into how a global semiconductor company runs enterprise-scale IT portfolio management.
What You Can Expect
Manage and track project status, timelines, and budgets across a portfolio of active IT initiatives, flagging risks and schedule slippage to project leads
Support stage-gate governance by preparing review materials, coordinating sessions, and following up on open action items
Partner with vendors and internal stakeholders to track progress, resolve delivery blockers, and keep milestones on schedule
Build and maintain dashboards and status reports that give leadership visibility into program health
Assist with documentation and continuous improvement of PMO templates, tools, and workflows
What We're Looking For
Currently enrolled in a Master's Degree (MBA) in Business Administration, Management, or a related field, with an expected graduation date of Fall 2027 – Summer 2028
Demonstrated experience managing multiple priorities or projects simultaneously in an academic, internship, or work setting
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to summarize complex information for varied audiences
Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint (or equivalent tools) for building trackers, dashboards, and presentations
Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage recurring deliverables against deadlines
Prior internship or coursework experience in project management, PMO, or IT/technology operations
Familiarity with project or portfolio management tools such as ServiceNow, Jira, or Smartsheet
Exposure to Agile/Scrum or Waterfall methodologies, or relevant PMP/CAPM coursework
Interest or coursework related to the semiconductor, hardware, or broader technology industry

Our AI Ecosystem team works across product, partner, and field organizations to help customers realize the full value of open source AI solutions. This summer, we’re looking for a motivated AI Ecosystem Intern to join our Boston-based team and help shape how Red Hat and our partners bring AI to market.
In this role, you will explore real-world AI opportunities by engaging directly with Red Hat partners and customer-facing teams. You’ll investigate critical customer AI use cases, map them to Red Hat’s AI platform and ecosystem capabilities, and identify potential partner motions to enhance our go-to-market (GTM) approach.

Conduct interviews with Red Hat partners, solution architects, and field sales teams to uncover the most pressing customer AI use cases
Analyze and synthesize findings to identify patterns, opportunities, and gaps in AI adoption
Map customer needs to Red Hat’s AI platform, open source technologies, and partner ecosystem capabilities
Recommend possible partner engagement strategies and motions that complement existing GTM efforts
Prepare and present a final report with recommendations to AI Ecosystem leadership

Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, data science, business, or a related field (expected graduation date December 2026 or later)

Excellent communication skills, especially in conducting interviews and presenting insights
Self-starter mindset with curiosity, adaptability, and a collaborative approach

Firsthand exposure to enterprise AI use cases and the open source AI landscape
Experience working at the intersection of technology, partners, and business strategy
Mentorship from Red Hat AI, partner, and GTM leaders
Opportunity to make strategic recommendations with real business impact

Job Description:
The Maintenance Operations Intern will support the day‑to‑day maintenance, reliability, and operational readiness of Repsol’s field equipment and production facilities. The intern will work closely with Maintenance Technicians, Field Operators, and Production teams to help ensure that equipment is safe, reliable, and operating efficiently.
This internship provides exposure to the mechanical systems, equipment inspections, reliability methods, and preventive maintenance strategies that support upstream and midstream oil and gas operations.
The intern will gain real‑world experience in:
Field Maintenance & Operations Exposure
How production equipment is operated, inspected, and maintained (compressors, engines, gensets, pumps, and other rotating equipment).
Routine and preventive maintenance tasks that support safe and reliable operations including hands-on tasks with technicians.
Assist technicians while diagnosing equipment issues and prioritizing corrective maintenance activities.
Mechanical & Reliability Fundamentals
Basic troubleshooting techniques for mechanical systems.
Understanding common failure modes and equipment reliability drivers.
Work Management & Maintenance Planning
How maintenance tasks are planned, scheduled, and executed.
Exposure to work orders, spare parts programs, and maintenance documentation.
How risk assessment and operating standards guide maintenance activities.
Cross‑Functional Collaboration
Interaction with Maintenance Engineering, Integrity Engineering, Production Engineering, HSE, and Field Operations teams.
How data and field observations support operational decisions and long‑term reliability planning.
Key Responsibilities
Field Operations & Mechanical Support
Participate in hands‑on maintenance activities within field operators related to rotating equipment (engines, compressors, gensets, and other equipment).
Assist with routine checks of production equipment and facility systems.
Help identify equipment needing repairs, calibration, or replacement.
Support reliability assessments by gathering field data and documenting equipment conditions.
Maintenance Program Support
Assist with developing or updating maintenance procedures, checklists, or standards.
Data, Documentation & Reporting
Help maintain maintenance records, equipment logs, and performance data.
Assist in developing reports related to equipment downtime, reliability, or maintenance activities.
Assist with predictive maintenance tools utilized to gather data on reciprocating compressors and engines
Project Work
Complete a summer-long project related to maintenance improvements, equipment reliability, digitalization, operational performance, or field/process optimization.
Present findings and recommendations to the Maintenance team and leadership at the end of the internship.

Fully authorized to work in the U.S. without sponsorship now or in the future. Additionally, we are not authorized for employment through OPT/CPT/F1 programs.
Currently enrolled in a 2 yr technical, engineering technology, or 4 yr engineering program.
GPA target: 3.0+ (flexible for technical college applicants).
Comfortable working in operating production facilities (repairing/maintaining equipment, wearing PPE).
Ability to work in loud environments and/or high ambient temperatures
Strong communication and teamwork skills.
Detail-oriented, organized, and safety‑aware.
Available locally in the Horseheads, NY (or Northern PA) region for the full 12-week term.

Industrial Maintenance
Mechanical Technology
Process Technology
Instrumentation/Controls
Petroleum Technology
Four‑year university students:
Mechanical Engineering
Petroleum Engineering
Industrial Engineering
Engineering Technology
Operations or Reliability‑focused programs
Required Skills
Mechanical curiosity and hands‑on aptitude
Comfort working within production facilities and around production equipment
Strong work ethic and reliability
Interest in understanding how field systems operate in real conditions

Business Process Audit and Advisory: Helps companies become more innovative by exploring their business processes, identifying and mitigating emerging risks, developing creative solutions to complex business challenges, and encouraging best practices to enhance business functions. Technology Audit and Advisory: Helps companies navigate the risks and opportunities of an increasingly complex technology landscape, including cybersecurity, AI risk, data governance, and cloud. Technology Auditors assess and advise across the full spectrum of how organizations use technology to protect and enhance enterprise value, including controls and regulatory compliance, privacy, software development, technology resilience, and technology governance.

Rather than assisting in the creation of the designs themselves, this role focuses on how those designs are taught.

Translate final creative direction into step-by-step digital manuals for stores, including:
Written build instructions
Material and prop checklists
Placement diagrams and callouts
Styling guidance and “Do / Don’t” examples
Help develop instructional video content, supporting script outlines, filming needs, and editing when able.
Organize large volumes of notes, visuals, and information into clean, digestible, magazine-style documents.
Ensure instructions balance design intent and practicality, making execution realistic for all store types.
Partner with teams to confirm clarity, accuracy, and consistency.
Maintain organized file systems and project folders, ensuring all documentation is easy to access and reference.

Someone with a love for layout, copy, graphic structure, and visual clarity
Someone who gets energy from turning creative chaos into beautifully simplified steps
Someone who wants to help others succeed by building tools that teach, guide, and empower
Qualifications
Junior, senior, or recent graduate majoring in Graphic Design, Visual Communication, Visual Merchandising, Editorial/Publication Design, Instructional Design, or related field
Strong skills in layout and visual organization (InDesign, Illustrator, Figma, or similar platforms preferred)
Excellent attention to detail in both visual polish and written grammar
Ability to simplify complex information into clear, actionable sequencing
Highly organized and comfortable managing multiple project deadlines simultaneously
Collaborative communicator who enjoys cross-department work
Why This Role Matters
Beautiful design becomes meaningful only when stores can bring it to life.
This role ensures that:
Every store receives tools that are inspiring, clear, and easy to follow
Execution consistency matches the creative vision
The guest experience feels elevated across every location, every season

Guest service fundamentals and experience building and managing a guest-first team culture across the store

At TC Energy, we are proud to connect the world to the energy it needs. Guided by our values of safety in every step, personal accountability, one team and active learning, we deliver the critical energy that North America and the world rely on while balancing reliability, affordability and sustainability.
Join us. Connect to what matters.
Work Term: May 2027 - August 2027
To be considered, applications must include a resume and unofficial academic transcript. Incomplete submissions may not be reviewed. We appreciate your attention to detail and look forward to learning more about you!
The Opportunity
We are seeking a Student Intern to support field operations related to the safe and reliable transportation of natural gas. In this role, you will gain hands-on experience working with natural gas compression equipment, field maintenance activities, troubleshooting processes, and operational procedures. The Student Intern will work alongside experienced technicians, participate in field projects and inspections, and develop practical technical skills that support the safe and efficient delivery of energy.
At TC Energy, connection is at the heart of everything we do. As a Student Intern, you will contribute to meaningful work that helps connect people, communities and industries to the energy they rely on every day. You will gain hands-on experience working alongside experienced professionals, applying your academic knowledge to real-world projects and helping support the safe and reliable delivery of energy across North America.
As a valued member of our team, you will take on challenging and rewarding work, build lasting professional relationships and develop skills that will help shape your future career. Through collaboration, mentorship and practical experience, you'll gain insight into our business while contributing to work that matters. Every day presents an opportunity to learn, grow and make an impact while helping power progress for the communities we serve.
What you'll do
Support field operations while demonstrating TC Energy's core values of Safety In Every Step, Personal Accountability, One Team, and Active Learning
Assist with the installation, maintenance, and troubleshooting of natural gas compressors and related equipment
Gain hands-on experience using field tools, equipment, and operational procedures
Learn and apply safety protocols and procedures for field work
Participate in site visits, equipment inspections, and project activities under supervision
Develop technical and problem-solving skills applicable to a field technician role
Minimum Qualifications
Currently enrolled in an accredited Mechanical, Chemical, Pipeline, Automation, or related technical / trades program
Completion of at least one academic term prior to the start of the work term in May 2027
Returning to full-time studies immediately following the work term
Availability to work full-time (40 hours per week) for the duration of the work term
Preferred Qualifications
Exposure to mechanical equipment maintenance, troubleshooting, or field operations through coursework or projects
Knowledge of natural gas compression systems, industrial equipment, or related technical fields
Demonstrate a safety mindset, in a professional and personal setting
Exhibit the TC Energy corporate values and incorporate them into work activities and initiatives
Strong interpersonal and communicative skills to work efficiently in a collaborative team environment
Commitment to building and maintaining relationships with internal and external stakeholders
Ability to accurately analyze information and deal with ambiguity
Experience working in a dynamic and challenging environment, and adaptable to changing priorities
Ability to multi-task effectively, with strong organizational and time management skills
Reflective and committed to continuous improvement and personal development
This position requires candidates to:
Successfully complete pre-employment medical screening including drug and alcohol testing
Relocation Eligibility
This position is eligible for our student relocation assistance program.
About our business
We are a leader in North American energy infrastructure, spanning Canada, the U.S. and Mexico. For over 75 years, we have proudly connected the world to the energy it needs. Every day, we move more than 30 per cent of the natural gas used across the continent and connect LNG exports to global markets, powering communities and industries. Complemented by strategic ownership and low-risk investments in power generation, our infrastructure delivers affordable, reliable and sustainable energy across North America. Our field operations span seven Canadian provinces, 34 U.S. states and seven Mexican states. Together, we strengthen the connections that deliver the energy the world relies on-every day.
TC Energy is an equal opportunity employer and participates in the E-Verify program supervised by the US government. We welcome applications from all qualified individuals regardless of race, religion, age, sex, color, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, or disability. We are also committed to providing accommodations throughout the recruitment process. Applicants requiring accommodations or accessible formats are encouraged to contact us at careers@tcenergy.com for support.
All applicants must have legal authorization to work in the country where the position is based, without restrictions. Background screening is required for all positions, which may include criminal and/or credit checks. Offers may be extended at a different level or job title that best aligns with the successful candidate's qualifications.
Learn more
Visit us at TCEnergy.com and connect with us on our social media channels for our latest news, employee stories, community activities, and other updates.
Thank you for considering TC Energy in your career journey.

Are you looking for an exciting job where you can put your skills and talents to work at a company you can feel proud to be a part of? Do you want a workplace that will challenge you and offer you opportunities to learn and grow? A position at Xcel Energy could be just what you’re looking for.
At Xcel Energy, our employees are the driving force behind our success. So we make sure that, here, you can be your best. Doing work that makes a difference for neighbors and communities. Working with a team you can count on to push you. Expanding skills, staying ready for change, and capturing opportunities to grow. All with the support, rewards and recognition you need to thrive – during your internship and beyond.
Work alongside experienced professionals to support electrical, instrumentation and controls, and mechanical maintenance functions at a nuclear facility. This role provides exposure to critical plant systems and real-world maintenance practices in a highly regulated environment.
Typical intern responsibilities may include but are not limited to:
Support electrical, instrument and controls and mechanical maintenance at a nuclear plant.
Set up a breaker tracking and tool checkout program with QR codes/scanners/PM program.
Collaborate maintenance feedback into optimizing preventative maintenance performance.
Analyzing feedback/observation data to identify trends and improve performance.
This position is for a May 24, 2027 start date. This position may have the possibility to extend beyond the internship’s initial term based on the candidate’s successful performance and Xcel Energy’s business needs.
Minimum Requirements:
Current student, Junior or higher
Enrolled in an accredited college or university and pursuing a degree in Electrical and Mechanical Engineering
Able to work full-time during the summer (up to 40 hours a week)/ part time during the school year (up to 20 hours a week) and commuting to the designated work location in-person, per our hybrid work policy.
Preferred Qualifications:
Interest in power plant/mechanical operations.
